# How to Advertise on Peacock: CTV Buying Options, Targeting and Creative Checklist





Oct 27, 2026





Programmatic Advertising





13 min read

Author: Ad Geeks Editorial Team

Updated: Oct 27, 2026

Published: Oct 27, 2026

> **Quick answer:** To advertise on Peacock, choose Universal Ads for self-service access, NBCUniversal One Platform for direct cross-platform packages, or an eligible DSP and deal for programmatic activation. Confirm that Peacock inventory is included, match targeting to available scale, submit exact-duration 16:9 video, and leave time for platform and publisher review approval.

If you are researching **how to advertise on Peacock**, the first decision is not the audience or creative. It is the buying route. Peacock inventory can sit inside a self-service marketplace, a direct NBCUniversal plan, or a programmatic deal. Each route changes the inventory, targeting, reporting, approval path and commercial terms you can expect.

This guide maps those options and shows what to verify before launch. It also explains where managed CTV planning, deal discovery and creative QA reduce risk.

## **Peacock advertising access at a glance**

Buying route

Best fit

What you control

What to verify

**Universal Ads self-service**

Smaller and mid-market advertisers that want a direct, hands-on setup

Objective, audience, location, bid, budget, schedule, frequency and standard video creative

Peacock or NBCU network availability, eligible placements, forecasting and account approval

**NBCUniversal direct or One Platform**

Brands needing premium content, live moments, sponsorships or cross-platform scale

Negotiated plan, audience strategy, content alignment, custom formats and measurement package

Minimum commitment, exact Peacock allocation, cancellation terms, reporting granularity and creative lead time

**Programmatic guaranteed or PMP**

Advertisers that need DSP workflow, deal controls and consolidated buying

DSP-side pacing, bidding, audiences, frequency and reporting within deal rules

Approved DSP, seller, deal type, floor or fixed price, device coverage, data rights and whether the deal is Peacock-specific

**Managed CTV buying**

Teams that want route comparison, deal sourcing, trafficking and QA handled together

Business goals and approvals, while a partner manages platform and publisher coordination

Transparent fees, account ownership, inventory proof, optimization rights and measurement scope

**Important:** do not treat “NBCUniversal inventory” as proof that every impression will run on Peacock. Ask for the network, app, content, device and deal-level detail your decision requires.

## **Option 1: buy through Universal Ads**

Universal Ads is Comcast’s self-service TV advertising platform. Its current site describes access to NBCUniversal and other premium publishers with no platform minimum spend. The interface follows a familiar campaign, ad set and ad structure.

Advertisers can choose between 2 main campaign types:

*   **Performance+:** the system optimizes delivery across eligible premium publishers toward awareness or conversion goals.
    
*   **Content Select:** the advertiser chooses genres or allowlisted publisher networks for greater placement control.
    

Content Select can include a network-level choice, but specific publisher access may require an account representative. That makes the pre-launch availability check essential. If Peacock is the objective, confirm it in the platform forecast or in writing before committing the media plan.

Universal Ads is useful when the team wants self-service control and standard CTV video. It also supports the Universal Ads Pixel for conversion signals. The platform recommends beginning with 1-2 targeting layers, a simple structure and enough time for delivery to stabilize.

## **Option 2: plan directly with NBCUniversal**

NBCUniversal’s One Platform brings linear and streaming inventory into a broader planning and activation framework. This route is relevant when Peacock is part of a larger NBCU schedule or when the plan needs premium content, live sports, sponsorships or custom ad innovation.

Direct plans can support strategic audiences, contextual alignment and negotiated measurement. They can also open formats beyond standard in-stream video. Peacock’s current advertising page highlights products such as Spotlight, contextual Pause Ads and Engagement Ads. Availability depends on the product, content window and commercial agreement.

This route usually needs more coordination. Ask the seller to separate Peacock delivery from the rest of the NBCU portfolio. Request impression, spend and outcome reporting at the lowest available level.

## **Option 3: activate a programmatic deal**

Programmatic access can use a private marketplace or programmatic guaranteed deal made available to an eligible DSP seat. NBCUniversal publicly describes programmatic activation within its ad tech stack. It has also opened selected premium events through biddable private marketplace access.

The practical rule is simple: **availability is deal-specific**. Do not assume Peacock is present in an open auction or in every DSP. Ask for these details before building the line item:

*   DSP and advertiser seat eligibility
    
*   Seller and supply path
    
*   Deal ID, deal type and pricing model
    
*   Peacock-only or broader NBCU inventory
    
*   Supported devices and environments
    
*   Geography, content and live-event restrictions
    
*   Audience permissions and frequency controls
    
*   Measurement, log-level data and reporting fields
    

A managed partner can compare direct, self-service and DSP routes before money moves. This is where Ad Geeks’ [CTV planning support](https://adgeeks.agency/solutions/ctv) fits: the plan starts with reachable inventory and verified access, not a preferred platform.

results.markdown:
Title: Google Ads Benchmarks for YOUR Industry [Updated!]

URL Source: https://www.wordstream.com/blog/ws/2016/02/29/google-adwords-industry-benchmarks

Published Time: 2016-02-19T05:00:00+00:00

Markdown Content:
Whether you’re doing PPC for the first time or you’ve just signed a new client, it can be daunting to know whether or not you’re doing a good job. Sure, we all want to create unicorn ads that have [highest CTRs](https://www.wordstream.com/blog/ws/2014/02/11/average-click-through-rate) and the [best conversion rates](https://www.wordstream.com/blog/ws/2014/03/17/what-is-a-good-conversion-rate), but what’s a good metric for one industry isn’t necessarily good for another. So what numbers should you be looking to beat in your industry?

Check out the Google Ads industry benchmarks our clients are seeing, including:

*   Average click-through rate (CTR)
*   Average cost per click (CPC)
*   Average conversion rate (CVR)
*   Average cost per action (CPA)

You’ll find averages across these ads metrics for twenty industries: Advocacy, Auto, B2B, Consumer Services, Dating & Personals, E-Commerce, Education, Employment Services, Finance & Insurance, Health & Medical, Home Goods, Industrial Services, Legal, Real Estate, Technology, and Travel & Hospitality.

**![Image 1: ✴️](https://s.w.org/images/core/emoji/17.0.2/svg/2734.svg) Note:**We update this data regularly! **[Download the PDF of our latest Google Ads Benchmarks report here](https://www.wordstream.com/resources/google-ads-industry-benchmarks?cid=Web_WS_InContent_Guide_GoogleAdsBenchmarks_Download&itm_source=wordstream&itm_medium=blog&itm_campaign=incontent_links).**

## Average Click-Through Rate in Google Ads by Industry

![Image 2: average ctr in adwords](https://www.wordstream.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/07/adwords-industry-benchmarks-average-ctr-3.png)

Dating and personal services really _click_ with PPC – boasting an average search CTR of 6%! No doubt, it’s easy to [write powerful emotional ad copy](https://www.wordstream.com/blog/ws/2015/11/09/emotional-ads) when your prospects are searching for love. Other industries with high search CTRs include Advocacy, Autos, and Travel.

When we first collected this data in 2015, legal services could struggle to attract attention on the SERP (with a relatively low average 1.35% CTR) – in large part due to [advertising restrictions](https://www.wordstream.com/blog/ws/2014/11/25/adwords-ad-disapproved) enforced by both Google and government organizations. [Legal advertisers](https://www.wordstream.com/blog/ws/2015/06/29/law-firm-marketing) have improved their stats in the past few years!

As of 2018, the industries with the lowest average click-through rates including Technology, B2B, and Consumer Services.

**The average click-through rate in Google Ads across all industries is 3.17% for search and 0.46% for display.**

Both of these averages are higher than they were a couple of years ago: Good news for Ads advertisers and agencies!

### Average Click Through Rate (CTR)

| Industry | Average CTR (Search) | Average CTR (GDN) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Advocacy | 4.41% | 0.59% |
| Auto | 4.00% | 0.60% |
| B2B | 2.41% | 0.46% |
| Consumer Services | 2.41% | 0.51% |
| Dating & Personals | 6.05% | 0.72% |
| E-Commerce | 2.69% | 0.51% |
| Education | 3.78% | 0.53% |
| Employment Services | 2.42% | 0.59% |
| Finance & Insurance | 2.91% | 0.52% |
| Health & Medical | 3.27% | 0.59% |
| Home Goods | 2.44% | 0.49% |
| Industrial Services | 2.61% | 0.50% |
| Legal | 2.93% | 0.59% |
| Real Estate | 3.71% | 1.08% |
| Technology | 2.09% | 0.39% |
| Travel & Hospitality | 4.68% | 0.47% |

![Image 3: 📙](https://s.w.org/images/core/emoji/17.0.2/svg/1f4d9.svg)**Free guide [>> Hacking Google Ads: One Trick That Could Save You Thousands](https://marketing.wordstream.com/WSLIQContentDLWebsiteHackingGoogleAds.html?cid=Web_Any_BlogInContent_PPC_HackingGoogleAds_Download)**

## Average Cost Per Click in Google Ads by Industry

![Image 4: contextual display costs](https://www.wordstream.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/07/adwords-industry-benchmarks-average-cpc-5.png)

It’s no surprise that legal services have some of the highest CPCs among all Google ads on the search network. Both “Lawyer” and “Attorney” make the top 10 [most expensive keywords on Google](https://www.wordstream.com/blog/ws/2011/07/18/most-expensive-keywords-google-adwords) and [on Bing](https://www.wordstream.com/blog/ws/2015/03/19/most-expensive-keywords-bing-ads). Average CPCs in the legal industry are over $6. Consumer services aren’t too far behind, with an average CPC of $6.40.

Advocacy and nonprofit groups are fortunate to have a cost per click under $2, likely as a result of the $2 max CPC bid [Google Grant advertisers](https://www.wordstream.com/blog/ws/2013/12/18/google-grants-adwords-for-nonprofits) have to set on all of their [keywords](https://www.wordstream.com/keywords).

Most industries have pretty inexpensive CPCs on the Google Display Network. The only industry with costs per click over $1 on the Display network is Dating & Personals.

**The average cost per click in Google Ads across all industries is $2.69 for search and $0.63 for display.**

The news here is good too: These [Google Ads costs](https://www.wordstream.com/blog/ws/2015/05/21/how-much-does-adwords-cost) have increased very little over the figures we found a couple of years ago (when the averages were $2.32 and $0.58 respectively).

### Average Cost Per Click (CPC)

| Industry | Average CPC (Search) | Average CPC (GDN) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Advocacy | $1.43 | $0.62 |
| Auto | $2.46 | $0.58 |
| B2B | $3.33 | $0.79 |
| Consumer Services | $6.40 | $0.81 |
| Dating & Personals | $2.78 | $1.49 |
| E-Commerce | $1.16 | $0.45 |
| Education | $2.40 | $0.47 |
| Employment Services | $2.04 | $0.78 |
| Finance & Insurance | $3.44 | $0.86 |
| Health & Medical | $2.62 | $0.63 |
| Home Goods | $2.94 | $0.60 |
| Industrial Services | $2.56 | $0.54 |
| Legal | $6.75 | $0.72 |
| Real Estate | $2.37 | $0.75 |
| Technology | $3.80 | $0.51 |
| Travel & Hospitality | $1.53 | $0.44 |

## Average Conversion Rates in Google Ads by Industry

![Image 5: average conversion rate in adwords](https://www.wordstream.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/07/adwords-industry-benchmarks-average-conversion-rate-2.png)

A couple of years ago, the Finance and Insurance industries were leading the pack when it came to conversion rates.

However, our newly updated data shows that the Dating & Personal industry is way out ahead now, with search conversion rates on average over 9%! Other standouts include the legal industries, consumer services, and autos.

In many of these cases, the best converting advertisers aren’t afraid to change their offer or their conversion flow to boost their conversion rates. Or they may be taking advantage of conversion-boosting tactics such as video landing pages.

results.title: About Display ads and the Google Display Network
results.markdown:
Title: About Display ads and the Google Display Network

URL Source: https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/2404190

Markdown Content:
We’re bringing the flexibility of standard Display campaigns and the AI capabilities of Smart Display campaigns into a single Display campaign. In addition to the existing benefits of Smart Display campaigns, you now have the ability to choose the level of AI integration that you prefer for bidding, creatives, and targeting.

Smart Display campaigns have been integrated into the standard Display campaign offering, enhancing them with AI-powered features. Any existing Smart Display campaigns in your account will have migrated to this unified Display campaign structure without any action needed on your part. This migration shouldn't cause any fluctuations in your campaign's performance. If you're looking to create a Smart campaign and can no longer find that option, this updated Display campaign is the successor, offering similar AI capabilities with more control. For other automated campaign types, consider Performance Max or Search campaigns. Learn more [About (newly simplified) Display campaigns](https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/12035738).

![Image 1](https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/sPzwT-Bqx1aPfz50W-D45GUr80uja1sxUU18uBPhSZpE7GsSzl07WUqSSyU1z-0mvE8=w150)[Display campaigns](https://support.google.com/google-ads/topic/10016807) serve visually engaging ads on the Google Display Network. The Display Network helps you reach people as they browse millions of websites, apps, and Google-owned properties (such as YouTube and Gmail).

Display campaigns offer a simple, intelligent solution to managing the complex variables of display advertising, and may be the most effortless way to broaden your customer base and win new conversions. Use a Display campaign to show ads in almost all formats across the Google Display Network, reaching people at all stages in the buying cycle—from people with demonstrated interests to customers just about to buy.

**On this page**

*   [Benefits](https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/2404190#Benefits)
*   [How the Google Display Network works](https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/2404190#How-the-Google-Display-Network-works)
*   [Get started on Responsive display ads](https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/2404190#Get-started-on-Responsive-display-ads)
*   [How Display ads work](https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/2404190#How-Display-ads-work)
*   [Keep in mind the Google Display Network timeline](https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/2404190#Keep-in-mind-the-Google-Display-Network-timeline)

## [Benefits](https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/2404190)

*   **Reach people in multiple places**: Display campaigns can reach people worldwide across 35 million websites and apps, and on Google-owned properties (YouTube and Gmail). This allows you to expand your reach beyond just Google Search.
*   **Build campaigns around your goals**: Drive sales, leads, and website traffic or build awareness and consideration for your business, product, or service.
*   **Designed for ease of use**: Display campaigns use AI-powered solutions across targeting, bidding, and formats to reach a new or existing audience. This can help your campaign deliver the best campaign results, friction-free. 
    *   **Optimized targeting**: Find the best performing audience segments that include potential customers with the highest likelihood to help you meet your conversion goals. [Learn more about optimized targeting](https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/10537509)
    *   **Smart bidding**: Bidding that uses AI to optimize for conversions or conversion value in each and every auction. It helps you save time and improve performance. [Learn more about Smart bidding](https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/7065882)

*   **A top-performing campaign in minutes**: You enter the building blocks for your ads—like headlines, images, and logos—and we’ll find you as many customers as we can within the CPA bid and budget you control.
*   **Smarter, not harder**: Display campaigns optimize within days. Google AI selects the best combination of assets to give your campaign the best performance. In this way, you can learn which of your headlines, descriptions, images, and logos perform best.

## [How the Google Display Network works](https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/2404190)

The Google Display Network helps you find the right audience with its targeting options that strategically show your message to potential customers at the right place and the right time. Display campaigns include AI capabilities that help improve campaign performance:

*   **Bidding**: [Smart Bidding strategies](https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/7065882) will be recommended to you based on your advertising goals. You can, however, choose not to use the suggested bidding strategies, and can manually select your bidding strategies. 
    *   **Pay for conversions**: You can pay for conversions, instead of clicks on Display campaigns that use Target CPA bidding. When setting up your campaign, go to the “Bidding” section. Look for the header labeled “Pay for” and select Conversions from the dropdown menu. Learn more [about pay for conversions](https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/7528254).

*   **Creatives**: By default, your [Display ads are responsive](https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/6363750) (unless you’re using uploaded Display ads). That means that you can upload different assets into Google Ads, and Google AI will determine the optimal combination of assets as well as the optimal size, appearance, and format of assets to fit available ad spaces with an ad format that is most likely to perform well.
*   **Targeting**: [Optimized targeting](https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/10537509) uses information such as keywords on your landing page to help you reach new and relevant audiences that are likely to convert. Optimized targeting is set as the default targeting method for your Display campaigns. If you prefer not to use optimized targeting, you can select a different form of targeting.

#### Optimize your campaign as you create it

As you create your campaign, you may receive notifications based on your setting selections. These notifications may alert you of issues that can result in decreased performance or that may be significant enough to prevent you from publishing your campaign.

The campaign construction navigation menu that appears as you construct your campaign provides a holistic view of your construction progress and will call attention to notifications that you may want to address. Move between steps in the navigation menu to easily review and resolve potential issues with your targeting, bidding, budget, or other campaign settings. Learn how to [Set up your campaign for success](https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/9451609).

## [Get started
